steps.text: Hi, I'm {name}! I'll show you around. This is the Learn page, where all your lessons are.
This is today's goal. Fill the ring a little every day and finish your daily quests.
Your streak and your tree live here. Each day you study, you can water the tree and watch it grow.
Tap this to start your next lesson. Ganbatte! (That means "you can do it!")
This road teaches every letter, one by one. Each row ends with a small test.
Switch between hiragana, katakana and the letters with marks (が, ぱ, きゃ) here.
Tap the glowing letter to learn it.
This is your tree! Study every day and it grows from a sprout into a blossoming sakura.
If you skip days, it dries out and loses its leaves. Don't worry: studying again brings them back.
Words you learn come back here for review just before you'd forget them. A few minutes a day is enough.
Here you write words by hand. I'll check your writing!
This is your page: your weekly progress, your rank and your trophies.
Your trophies, ranking, tips and settings are here. Reviews, speaking and stories live in the Practice tab. Tap the ? at any time to see my tips again.
New things to learn look like this. Tap the speaker to hear it, then tap Got it.
Pick an answer, then tap Check. Stuck? The light bulb at the top gives you a hint.
Tap a card on one side, then its partner on the other side, until every pair is matched.
Trace the grey letter with your finger, one letter in each box. Use Next for the following box, then tap Check.
Tap the word tiles in the right order to build the sentence. Tap a tile again to take it back.
Listen, then write what you hear. Tap the speaker to hear it again.
Tap the microphone and say the line out loud. Don't be shy!
Type how it sounds in English letters (romaji), then tap Check.
Welcome to Lesson+! Here you learn the words and phrases for real situations, like ordering food or asking the way.
Type a situation here, for example "restaurant" or "train", and I'll find lessons for it.
These are real Japanese videos. Each one has subtitles you can tap, with romaji and English.
Search for a topic here. Start with the "For beginners" row if you're new.
This is katakana! It has the same sounds as hiragana but sharper shapes. It's used for words from other languages, like コーヒー (koohii, coffee) and テレビ (terebi, TV).
This is hiragana, the first script every learner starts with. It writes Japanese words and grammar, like ありがとう (arigatou, thank you).
Two little marks change a sound: か (ka) becomes が (ga), and は (ha) becomes ぱ (pa). Small や, ゆ, よ blend sounds too: き + ゃ = きゃ (kya).
This is the whole chart in one table. Tap any letter to hear it. Letters you've learned are coloured in.

faq.q: What are hiragana, katakana and kanji?
faq.a: Japanese uses three scripts together. Hiragana writes Japanese words and grammar. Katakana writes words from other languages. Kanji are characters with meanings, like 山 for mountain. Start with hiragana, then katakana.

faq.q: How does my sakura tree grow?
faq.a: Each day you finish a lesson, your watering can fills up. Water your tree and it grows, from a sprout all the way to a blossoming sakura. If you skip days, its petals fall, but studying again brings them back.

faq.q: How do I write in the boxes?
faq.a: Write one character in each box with your finger. Tap Next to move to the next box, then tap Check. At first you trace grey letters; once you know a word, you write it on your own.
Words you learn come back for review just before you'd forget them. Doing a few reviews every day moves them into long-term memory. Find them in Practice on the Me page.

faq.q: Can I skip what I already know?
faq.a: Yes! Take the placement test from Settings, or tap Test out on any unit. If you pass, those lessons are marked as done.

demo.title: Hi, I'm {name}!
demo.text: I'll be your guide. Together we'll learn Japanese from your very first letter.

demo.title: Read, write and speak
demo.text: Learn hiragana, katakana and kanji step by step. Write by hand and I'll check it, and practise saying real phrases.

demo.title: Grow your sakura
demo.text: Study a little every day and your cherry tree grows with you. Ready? Let's begin!

about: Your guide. Poses: wave, point, cheer, think. Put guide/<character id>/<pose>.webp (or .png) in assets to replace the drawn character with artwork. Steps may set "side": "left" or "right"; otherwise she stands on the side away from what she points at. Write {name} where the guide says their own name. "voices" lists the text-to-speech voices each character prefers, best first, by engine id (Google's ids here); the first one installed on the phone is used, otherwise the phone's default voice at the character's pitch.
